  "title": "Currently not GDPR compliant - reason external fonts",
  "body": "## Description\r\n\r\nAs in EU the GDPR starts to be active from May 25th on. It would be good if all external fonts and services are part of the bundle and do not link to the CDN version. Otherwise we have to display a cookie consent and a privacy policy for a \"documentation\".  \r\n\r\n### Expected behavior\r\n\r\nPlease include the Material Icons and Roboto Font directly (and other external services) into the bundle at least everything which is needed for the default material theme.\r\nCurrently it is not GDPR compliant how it is right now.\r\n\r\n### Actual behavior\r\n\r\nIt's loaded from a CDN.\r\n\r\n### Steps to reproduce the bug\r\n\r\nIn the Base.html (maybe in other files as well) from the material design there are links to the CDN services.",
  "author": "Participant 1",
  "created_at": "2018-03-19T17:56:48Z",
  "updated_at": "2022-11-14T15:33:47Z",
  "state": "closed",

      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "Google Fonts [don't use](https://developers.google.com/fonts/faq#what_does_using_the_google_fonts_api_mean_for_the_privacy_of_my_users) Cookies though?"
    },
    {
      "id": 374330957,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-374330957",
      "created_at": "2018-03-19T19:06:30Z",
      "updated_at": "2019-06-28T17:07:50Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "I'm a European citizen and highly critize the EU for issueing such a half-baked law. It will cost companies millions in implementation and legal fees. It's impractical to host everything by yourself. Is it even allowed to self-host Google Fonts per their license? Don't really know if I want to take any action here."
    },
    {
      "id": 374532915,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-374532915",
      "created_at": "2018-03-20T09:38:14Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "@wopian yes thats true, they are not using cookie, but they get the IP-address from the user. \r\nBut the font awesome icons are setting a cookie, as there are hosted on cloudflare (partials/social.html).\r\n\r\n@squidfunk Yes I aggree, but still as company we have to deal with it as it is. For our side we adapted the base.html and the social.html and downloaded the necessary fonts to the assets folder.\r\n\r\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 374556286,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-374556286",
      "created_at": "2018-03-20T10:59:08Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "@DsrMedia: I totally understand. \r\n\r\nHowever, self-hosting all assets would mean we would need to keep everything in sync. Also when self-hosting Google Fonts we may loose rendering quality because Google's CDN serves distinct files for Windows and macOS for optimization reasons. You can disable Google Fonts entirely as described in the getting started guide.\r\n\r\nWe could host FontAwesome by ourselves, as it's pinned to a specific version and upgrading to 5 would mean a major release of the theme because class names / qualifiers changed. Would that help?"
    },
    {
      "id": 374556917,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-374556917",
      "created_at": "2018-03-20T11:01:21Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 4",
      "body": "@squidfunk FYI http://michaelboeke.com/blog/2013/09/10/Self-hosting-Google-web-fonts/"
    },
    {
      "id": 374558965,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-374558965",
      "created_at": "2018-03-20T11:08:31Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "Oh and we would loose the ability to easily change the font face per configuration or would have to bundle all fonts."
    },
    {
      "id": 374973514,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-374973514",
      "created_at": "2018-03-21T15:13:40Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-05-31T16:33:48Z",
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "**Edit**: This is not legal advice, and does **not** mean you can continue using Google Fonts in your project. \r\n\r\nI did some research and found a few links to point that it should not be a problem to use Google Fonts even after GDPR takes effect.\r\n\r\n1. [Google Fonts FAQ Section on Privacy](https://developers.google.com/fonts/faq#what_does_using_the_google_fonts_api_mean_for_the_privacy_of_my_users)\r\n\r\n2. [Discussion on GDPR Compliance](https://github.com/google/fonts/issues/1495) on the Google Fonts GitHub Repository\r\n\r\n3. [Google GDPR Compliance Notice](https://privacy.google.com/businesses/compliance/#?modal_active=none)\r\n\r\nI strongly believe that we should continue using Google Fonts, because it offers fast content distribution and optimizations as mentioned by @squidfunk \r\n\r\nGoogle should be releasing a statement of compliance soon."
    },
    {
      "id": 377978270,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-377978270",
      "created_at": "2018-04-02T16:59:14Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "Yes, we will definitely be using Google Fonts at least until May 25, and then reconsider how we use/advertise it depending on the statement of compliance Google will hopefully be issuing soon.\r\n\r\nI will close this issue for now because there's nothing that can be done right at the moment. Furthermore, Google Fonts can be disabled easily by setting the following parameter in `mkdocs.yml`:\r\n\r\n```yml\r\ntheme:\r\n  font: false\r\n```"
    },
    {
      "id": 393568225,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-393568225",
      "created_at": "2018-05-31T15:26:00Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "@squidfunk Considering your completely immature response to this, which leaves users up to liability, I am very disappointed in this project.\r\n\r\nFor my own use cases I have now created a fork that does not use Google Fonts."
    },
    {
      "id": 393586700,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-393586700",
      "created_at": "2018-05-31T16:14:17Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "> @squidfunk Considering your completely immature response to this, which leaves users up to liability, I am very disappointed in this project.\r\n\r\nIf you mean my initial reaction: I think GDPR is great in theory but is an entire gray area as there are no official judgments or guidelines what is okay and what is not.\r\n\r\nIf you mean my intention to wait until it's clear what to do I cannot understand your anger. Google Fonts can be easily disabled and replaced by self hosted fonts (see my last comment) and there's definitely a plan to include FontAwesome into the distribution files (but that's only CSS, so probably not as critical as Google Analytics)."
    },
    {
      "id": 393589452,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-393589452",
      "created_at": "2018-05-31T16:21:37Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "@squidfunk I mean your entire attitude towards a privacy and legal issue, which is \"I don’t care\". Completely disregarding the users that are affected by it.\r\n\r\nI can’t trust a project that might end up sending user’s data to who-knows-where because \"it can be easily disabled and replaced\"."
    },
    {
      "id": 393594514,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-393594514",
      "created_at": "2018-05-31T16:36:16Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "Okay, I see your point. Actually it's not that I don't care, I'm very aware of the issue. The problem is that many people are using Material and the changes that we discussed would have quite an impact. My aim is to keep things as stable and constant as possible. For this reason we decided to settle until we know how to implement this with maximum compatibility and optimal usability. I'm very concerned about usability.\r\n\r\nCould you make a constructive proposal how we could comply with GDPR and keep Material easy to use? Also, is Google Fonts not GDPR compliant? Did someone have the time to study this topic?"
    },
    {
      "id": 393594951,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-393594951",
      "created_at": "2018-05-31T16:37:44Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "I think we should issue a statement in the docs on GDPR compliance of Material and how to achieve it."
    },
    {
      "id": 393596421,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-393596421",
      "created_at": "2018-05-31T16:42:57Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "There's been a lot of debate about this on the Google Fonts repository issue that I linked before. Although Google has issued several official statements (prefixed to the first comment), but these statements do not directly address the problem, and do not make it clear as to whether we can use Fonts in projects.\r\n\r\n[This discussion](https://github.com/CIDRAM/CIDRAM/issues/66) on CIDRAM proposes to disable use of Google Fonts by default and add a clause to the Privacy Policy about enabling it.\r\n\r\nAgain, this is not legal advice, and we need to be careful!"
    },
    {
      "id": 393597400,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-393597400",
      "created_at": "2018-05-31T16:46:10Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "Thanks! What about if we include the default Roboto font family with the Material distribution, so by default Material would not query the Google Fonts CDN. If the fonts are set via `mkdocs.yml`, we would link to Google Fonts and add an Admonition to the docs that this possibly breaks GDPR compliance. Font Awesome will be directly included. This way all external dependencies could be eliminated by default and the UX would stay the same.\r\n\r\nAny thoughts?"
    },
    {
      "id": 393601040,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-393601040",
      "created_at": "2018-05-31T16:58:19Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "I believe this is what we should do till Google and other providers clear the issue.\r\n\r\nCan the `font` parameter be programmed to enable/disable CDN for Font Awesome, too? There may be developers who may decide not to disable CDN, for faster loading."
    },
    {
      "id": 393604590,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-393604590",
      "created_at": "2018-05-31T17:09:54Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "That would be appreciated, yes. For now I’ve taken down my sites that use this until the issue is resolved. (But I’d want to keep an option to stick with entirely self-hosted everything even if Google sorts this out, and especially without any analytics or tracking)."
    },
    {
      "id": 393606263,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-393606263",
      "created_at": "2018-05-31T17:15:20Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "> Can the font parameter be programmed to enable/disable CDN for Font Awesome, too? There may be developers who may decide not to disable CDN, for faster loading.\r\n\r\nThat makes it more complicated so I would favor always including it. However, you could always override the theme."
    },
    {
      "id": 393606393,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-393606393",
      "created_at": "2018-05-31T17:15:48Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "@justjanne: just disable Google Fonts and you are fine! No need to take it down."
    },
    {
      "id": 393607514,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-393607514",
      "created_at": "2018-05-31T17:19:26Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-05-31T17:20:01Z",
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "@squidfunk If I disable Google Fonts, all icons will be missing and more.\r\n\r\nI already am running a heavily modified version here so I can get KaTeX support (instead of MathJax – ideally I’d even be able to get KaTeX at build time, but that’s a bit more work), and so I can change a few other minor details (e.g. making the icon at the top of the docs link back to the main site of the project instead of the docs home)\r\n\r\nSo, I’ve taken it all down for now, and then I’ll wait until the fix, merge it into my version, and run that."
    },
    {
      "id": 393612063,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-393612063",
      "created_at": "2018-05-31T17:33:45Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 12",
      "body": "Wouldn't having the information be available, albeit not pretty, be much preferred to unavailable completely? @justjanne \r\n\r\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 394088772,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-394088772",
      "created_at": "2018-06-02T13:45:23Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "My current plan to ensure GDPR compliance is the following:\r\n\r\n- Bundle Material Icons with Material for self-hosting by default\r\n- Bundle Font Awesome 4 by default (upgrade to version 5 is another task)\r\n- Bundle Roboto 400 and 700, as well as Roboto Mono 400 with theme\r\n\r\nThis should ensure GDPR compliance for the default configuration - meaning no custom fonts, no analytics – no third-party at all. I will also add documentation for this. If the user changes the fonts, Google Fonts will be used. This will also be noted in the docs. This will make the following option obsolete:\r\n\r\n```\r\ntheme:\r\n  font: false\r\n```\r\n\r\nIt will be deprecated with 3.0, as no fonts are loaded by default.\r\n\r\nAny thoughts?"
    },
    {
      "id": 394734449,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-394734449",
      "created_at": "2018-06-05T14:38:42Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 13",
      "body": "I think it would also be helpful to briefly explain how to include other fonts without using google fonts.\r\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 396045729,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-396045729",
      "created_at": "2018-06-10T12:35:38Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-06-10T12:35:51Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "So this is turning out harder than I thought. The problem is the way Google Fonts serves web fonts - they analyze the user agent and serve the ideal compatible web font format. For each requested font weight they serve 7 font face definitions for different charsets, e.g. `latin`, `cyryllic`, etc:\r\n\r\n``` css\r\n/* cyrillic-ext */\r\n@font-face {\r\n  font-family: 'Roboto';\r\n  font-style: italic;\r\n  font-weight: 400;\r\n  src: local('Roboto Italic'), local('Roboto-Italic'), url(https://fonts.gstatic.com/s/roboto/v18/KFOkCnqEu92Fr1Mu51xFIzIXKMnyrYk.woff2) format('woff2');\r\n  unicode-range: U+0460-052F, U+1C80-1C88, U+20B4, U+2DE0-2DFF, U+A640-A69F, U+FE2E-FE2F;\r\n}\r\n/* cyrillic */\r\n@font-face {\r\n  font-family: 'Roboto';\r\n  font-style: italic;\r\n  font-weight: 400;\r\n  src: local('Roboto Italic'), local('Roboto-Italic'), url(https://fonts.gstatic.com/s/roboto/v18/KFOkCnqEu92Fr1Mu51xMIzIXKMnyrYk.woff2) format('woff2');\r\n  unicode-range: U+0400-045F, U+0490-0491, U+04B0-04B1, U+2116;\r\n}\r\n/* greek-ext */\r\n@font-face {\r\n  font-family: 'Roboto';\r\n  font-style: italic;\r\n  font-weight: 400;\r\n  src: local('Roboto Italic'), local('Roboto-Italic'), url(https://fonts.gstatic.com/s/roboto/v18/KFOkCnqEu92Fr1Mu51xEIzIXKMnyrYk.woff2) format('woff2');\r\n  unicode-range: U+1F00-1FFF;\r\n}\r\n/* greek */\r\n@font-face {\r\n  font-family: 'Roboto';\r\n  font-style: italic;\r\n  font-weight: 400;\r\n  src: local('Roboto Italic'), local('Roboto-Italic'), url(https://fonts.gstatic.com/s/roboto/v18/KFOkCnqEu92Fr1Mu51xLIzIXKMnyrYk.woff2) format('woff2');\r\n  unicode-range: U+0370-03FF;\r\n}\r\n/* vietnamese */\r\n@font-face {\r\n  font-family: 'Roboto';\r\n  font-style: italic;\r\n  font-weight: 400;\r\n  src: local('Roboto Italic'), local('Roboto-Italic'), url(https://fonts.gstatic.com/s/roboto/v18/KFOkCnqEu92Fr1Mu51xHIzIXKMnyrYk.woff2) format('woff2');\r\n  unicode-range: U+0102-0103, U+0110-0111, U+1EA0-1EF9, U+20AB;\r\n}\r\n/* latin-ext */\r\n@font-face {\r\n  font-family: 'Roboto';\r\n  font-style: italic;\r\n  font-weight: 400;\r\n  src: local('Roboto Italic'), local('Roboto-Italic'), url(https://fonts.gstatic.com/s/roboto/v18/KFOkCnqEu92Fr1Mu51xGIzIXKMnyrYk.woff2) format('woff2');\r\n  unicode-range: U+0100-024F, U+0259, U+1E00-1EFF, U+2020, U+20A0-20AB, U+20AD-20CF, U+2113, U+2C60-2C7F, U+A720-A7FF;\r\n}\r\n/* latin */\r\n@font-face {\r\n  font-family: 'Roboto';\r\n  font-style: italic;\r\n  font-weight: 400;\r\n  src: local('Roboto Italic'), local('Roboto-Italic'), url(https://fonts.gstatic.com/s/roboto/v18/KFOkCnqEu92Fr1Mu51xIIzIXKMny.woff2) format('woff2');\r\n  unicode-range: U+0000-00FF, U+0131, U+0152-0153, U+02BB-02BC, U+02C6, U+02DA, U+02DC, U+2000-206F, U+2074, U+20AC, U+2122, U+2191, U+2193, U+2212, U+2215, U+FEFF, U+FFFD;\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nAs Material is a theme used in many different languages, we cannot possibly exclude any of the definitions. This means that for each weight, we would need to include 7 font face definitions. Additionally, this is only `woff2` format - we would also need to serve `woff` and `ttf` at least (possibly `eot` if we want to support older IEs, but let's just forget about that). Material currently loads the weights 300, 400, 400i, 700 for Roboto and 400 for Roboto Mono, so 5 web fonts in total.\r\n\r\nThe total amount of webfonts to be bundled with Material is:\r\n\r\n5 (weights) x 7 (charsets) x 3 (formats) = 105 web font files. Impractical.\r\n\r\nI don't really know how we should proceed. I'm currently thinking of dropping Roboto for the default configuration (however still to be enabled via `mkdocs.yml` to use Google Fonts) and fall back to Helvetica or the respective system font. This would make Material GDPR compliant in its default configuration and still leave the possibility to use webfonts.\r\n\r\nPersonally, I think, from a user perspective, it may be better to leave the Google Font loading as-is (to be disabled via `theme.font: false`) and bundle all icons fonts. This way GDPR compliance can be ensured with a single line, but the default user experience is not crippled as it would with falling back to system fonts.\r\n\r\nAny thoughts?"
    },
    {
      "id": 396045972,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-396045972",
      "created_at": "2018-06-10T12:40:11Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "> I think it would also be helpful to briefly explain how to include other fonts without using google fonts.\r\n\r\n@vbd: you can just override the `fonts` block with your own `link` and `style` tags, see:\r\nhttps://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/customization/#overriding-template-blocks\r\n\r\nThis is the default code generated by the block - you would have to provide your own definitions here:\r\n\r\nhttps://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/blob/2fbeb28d9dbda3e27fbe78dfa7cd53e76db8dab2/src/base.html#L116-L138"
    },
    {
      "id": 396046442,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-396046442",
      "created_at": "2018-06-10T12:46:37Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "That is a lot of font files!\r\n\r\n[More discussion about Google Fonts](https://www.lifehacker.com.au/2018/06/how-to-be-gdpr-compliant-if-you-use-google-fonts-on-your-website/)\r\n\r\nYour idea of leaving the Google Fonts loading as-is makes much more sense now. Roboto is at the heart of Material Design, after all.\r\n\r\nIf that is being done, clear warnings could be added to the docs, along with the directive required to disable it."
    },
    {
      "id": 396046737,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-396046737",
      "created_at": "2018-06-10T12:50:11Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "Yes, I will provide an entire section on GDPR compliance and how to achieve it with Material"
    },
    {
      "id": 396062155,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-396062155",
      "created_at": "2018-06-10T16:28:10Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "2.8.0 was just released which bundles both icon fonts. This means that the font configuration option and GA and Disqus integration are the only things that break GDPR compliance. The first must be explicitly disabled, the latter both are disabled by default. See the new section on compliance and feel free to ask any questions so we can mark this topic as done.\r\n\r\nSee https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/compliance/"
    },
    {
      "id": 396578114,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-396578114",
      "created_at": "2018-06-12T12:51:59Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "Closing this as fixed. In case any issues or problems arise, feel free to re-open."
    },

      "id": 473548497,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-473548497",
      "created_at": "2019-03-16T15:36:33Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 14",
      "body": "@squidfunk As a lurker just have to saw your communication and resolution was stellar. Thanks for this?"
    },

    {
      "id": 1027430082,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-1027430082",
      "created_at": "2022-02-02T00:24:06Z",
      "updated_at": "2022-02-02T00:44:56Z",
      "author": "Participant 10",
      "body": "Please let me know if I'm missing something, but would it not be possible bundle Roboto in weights `300` `400` `400i` `700` and Roboto Mono weight `400` both in charsets `vietnamese` `latin-ext` `latin` `greek` `cyrillic-ext` `cyrillic` with the format of `woff2` and still cover [all browsers currently supported](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/browser-support/)? I believe it would involve 5 font files of total ~240KB. Including `woff` as well would make it a total of 10 font files and ~540KB.\r\n\r\nIt appears `woff2` is currently supported by [~94.9%](https://caniuse.com/woff2) of user's browsers, with `woff` at [96.7%](https://caniuse.com/woff).\r\n\r\n[Roboto](https://google-webfonts-helper.herokuapp.com/fonts/roboto?subsets=cyrillic,cyrillic-ext,greek,greek-ext,latin,latin-ext,vietnamese), [Roboto Mono](https://google-webfonts-helper.herokuapp.com/fonts/roboto-mono?subsets=cyrillic,cyrillic-ext,greek,latin,latin-ext,vietnamese) (note the 'Modern Browsers' option).\r\n\r\nOnly reason I'm mentioning that is, it's much more practical than the previously mentioned bundling of 105 font files and their corresponding CSS. I understand that the browsers you support has probably modernised since 2018 and that's likely why we can get away with only 1 or 2 font formats now, that and the combining of multiple charsets into a single font file.\r\n\r\nI would understand if you still preferred not to bundle these, as I know it would be another dependency when building (although updates to [the font itself](https://github.com/googlefonts/roboto) are infrequent), and the increase of either 240KB or 540KB for the project. Another aspect is the request from the browser itself to the web server will now be asking for more data directly, whereas it would have got a quick CDN or browser cache hit if using Google Fonts."
    },
    {
      "id": 1027713955,
      "url": "https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-1027713955",
      "created_at": "2022-02-02T08:55:21Z",
      "updated_at": "2022-02-03T08:38:20Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "@ajh0912 this is exactly what I analyzed it https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-396045729. You would have two options.\r\n\r\n**1. Bundle all variants**\r\n\r\n- 4 regular weights + 2 monospace weights (400 and 700, as sometimes code is rendered bold)\r\n- 2 formats (`woff` + `woff2`)\r\n- 6 charsets\r\n\r\n= 48 font files. At least. The numbers in the linked comment are higher because I included more weights and charsets. Remember that Material for MkDocs is used in [50+ languages](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/setup/changing-the-language/#configuration), so we cannot possibly loose support for some languages by removing some character sets, we need to support all of them to some degree.\r\n\r\n**2. Bundle woff/ttf including all charsets**\r\n\r\n`Roboto-Regular.ttf` weighs `164kb`. Take that times 6 (4 + 2 weights), you're at `984kb`. `woff` and `woff2` are possibly a little smaller than `ttf`, but not an order of magnitude. Currently, Material for MkDocs without fonts weighs `58kb` (gzipped), i.e. all CSS and JS sources. `woff` and `woff2` cannot be gzipped, as they're binary formats. Each font loaded from Google fonts adds `11kb` per font, so a total of around `66kb` for all fonts (for the regular `latin` charset), leading to:\r\n\r\n- `58kb` + `66kb` = `124kb` using Google Gonts\r\n- `58kb`+ `984kb` = `1042kb` using bundled `ttf` fonts\r\n\r\nThat's an order of magnitude, and only for Roboto, so you would be locked in to use this font.\r\n\r\n**Recommendation**\r\n\r\n[Turn font loading off](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/setup/changing-the-fonts/#monospaced-font) and fall back to system fonts. If that's not an option, you can download the font files and [bundle them yourself](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/setup/changing-the-fonts/#additional-fonts), but your website will likely receive worse scores on Lighthouse and/or Google.\r\n\r\n**Personal opinion**\r\n\r\nThis ruling is pretty interesting because it would mean that all use of CDNs without the visitor's consent could be considered \"leaking the visitors IP\", at least as I read it. Thus, all use of external assets (not services, assets!), be it from third-party cookie consent providers, analytics integrations, etc., basically, everything hosted on external servers must be considered problematic at least. I believe that this ruling will not be persistent. Thus, I would be patient and wait for how this is handled.\r\n\r\nNote that this is my personal opinion and I'm not an expert in legal affairs, but it might help to understand my argument.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\nDisclaimer: those numbers are estimates, so the actual numbers might be a little off, but the ratio roughly stays the same."
    },

      "updated_at": "2022-02-20T19:00:10Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "__Insiders 4.9.0__ adds a new plugin: the [__built-in privacy plugin__](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/setup/ensuring-data-privacy/) – the plugin will automatically download all external scripts, style and web fonts, so you can self-host them as part of your documentation without manual effort. The idea is to make compliance with GDPR easier, given the latest developments when serving external assets to users without prior consent.\r\n\r\nActivate it via `mkdocs.yml` with:\r\n\r\n``` yml\r\nplugins:\r\n  - privacy\r\n```\r\n\r\n\r\nThis was really tough. I'm very interested in your feedback, but the plugin should at least solve the font hosting problem once and for all. I've investigated and it seems that we only need `*.woff2`, since this covers the whole range of browsers that we are [officially supporting](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/browser-support/).\r\n\r\nOf course, it's still possible to achieve self-hosting manually without the use of the plugin, which I described in my last comment. The cool thing is that the plugin will download all assets regardless of where they are defined – in the template, as additional JavaScript or style sheets, or in Markdown – when they're external, they're downloaded."
    },
